promptName: Copilot Prompt: Recreate Portfolio-v3 With a New UI/UX
role: GitHub Copilot acting as a senior front-end/full-stack engineer
goal: Recreate the existing Portfolio-v3 project structure and technical stack as closely as possible, but give the site a noticeably different UI/UX direction and make only minor backend changes where needed.
principles: Preserve the original product scope, code organization, and dependency set.
Deliver a distinctly different visual identity and interaction model.
Keep the architecture simple, data-driven, and production-ready.
hardRequirements: Keep the same overall tech stack.
Keep the same core folder structure under src/.
Keep the same major dependencies and install equivalents.
Preserve the same app-router-based Next.js architecture.
Keep the same main content sections.
Preserve the same API route surface, but minor backend changes are allowed.
Keep the chatbot concept, but it should remain lightweight and local.
preserveFeatures: Hero section with strong headline treatment and motion.
Experience section with timeline or stacked cards.
Skills section with grouped proficiency indicators.
Projects section with rich project cards.
Contact section with a working form.
Custom cursor and loading screen if they still improve the UX.

uiUxDirection.style: Create a distinctly different design language instead of recreating the original visual style.
suggestedDirection: Use a more editorial or gallery-like composition.
Introduce stronger visual hierarchy in the hero.
Use asymmetric section layouts where useful.
Use purposeful gradients, texture, or layered backgrounds.
Make animations smoother but less noisy than the original.
Ensure the mobile experience is first-class.

behavior: Store or forward signup data in the same general way.
Keep the flow robust and user-friendly.

allowedChanges: Refactor utility code in src/lib/ if needed.
backendExpectations.constraint: Do not introduce unnecessary backend complexity.

Navbar: Preserve anchor navigation to the main sections.
Use a compact and elegant mobile interaction pattern.
Hero: Make this the strongest visual moment on the page.
Use layered typography, motion, and clear CTAs.
About: Present the narrative in a refined way, not a plain text block.
Experience: Show roles, companies, durations, and descriptions clearly.
Use motion and spacing to support readability.
Skills: Render grouped skill categories with a visible sense of progression.
Keep the content shape familiar even if the visual style changes.
Projects: Present projects as visually rich cards.
Keep external links and project metadata.
Reuse ProjectCard.tsx if it still fits the new design.
Contact: Use validation and user feedback that feel modern and clean.
ChatbotWidget: Keep the chatbot local and lightweight.
Read from src/data/content.ts instead of relying on a remote AI API.
Keep responses short, point-based, and useful.
Support English, Hindi, and Hinglish if the original content model expects that.
LoadingScreen: If kept, make it brief and tasteful.
It should not block the site longer than necessary.
CustomCursor: Keep only if it genuinely improves the new UX.
It should never hurt mobile usability.
ProgressBar: Keep if it supports the page narrative.
The implementation should be subtle and performant.

stylingRules: Use Tailwind CSS utility classes as the primary styling method.
Keep src/app/globals.css for global variables, resets, and foundational theming.
Maintain good spacing and responsive breakpoints.
Prefer reusable design tokens over one-off style hacks.
motionRules: Use Framer Motion for page transitions, section reveals, and card entrances.
Motion should support the content, not distract from it.
Keep animations performant on mid-range devices.
seoMetadata: Preserve or improve metadata in layout.tsx.
Keep canonical, Open Graph, and Twitter card support.
Ensure the preview image and title are meaningful.
qualityBar: Keep code readable and easy to extend.
Do not add dependencies unless they are already in the project stack.
outputExpectations: Uses the same stack and dependency family.
Preserves the same route and component structure.
Has a noticeably different visual design.
Keeps the backend behavior compatible with the original flows.
optionalImplementationNotes: If overlapping UI roles exist, consolidate only where it improves maintainability.
Keep the chatbot and notification flows simple and predictable.
If a component is not essential to the new UX, simplify it instead of removing the feature.
If backend utilities are refactored, keep the public route contracts stable.
